fact: Guinea inaugurated the Simandou Academy at the Transform Africa Summit, a training institution that will serve as a hub for digital skills and capacity enhancement, per Biometric Update.

TechAfrica News reports the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy and ANSUTEN launched the third edition of the R-CUN digital capacity building programme on 7 October 2025, after two editions that trained 450 young people, aiming to train 1,500 students; no second location is named for the programme.

Guinea approved the feasibility study for a National Digital Academy under the Simandou 2040 strategy, with a ministry official saying it should improve digital skills across a large share of the population; its courses and operating model are not yet defined.

ANSUTEN, under the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy, launched on 7 October 2025 the third edition of its R-CUN digital capacity programme for over 1,500 participants, with 30-day trainings across the country after two earlier editions of 450.

ANSUTEN's director general said the R-CUN digital capacity programme, run since 2022 through the Hub numerique, has trained more than 3,200 people, about 40 per cent women, and launched its fourth edition on 7 October 2026 aiming at over 2,000 beneficiaries.
system: R-CUN (Programme de renforcement des capacites a l'usage du numerique)
